art.title: View of Delft
art.credit: Public domain · image via Wikimedia Commons (Mauritshuis)
art.story: Vermeer's home town seen from across the water on a still morning after rain. Heavy clouds drift across a pale sky over the red roofs; the clock on the town gate says ten past seven; barges are moored along the quay, and a few people chat on the sandy bank. Behind it all, sunlight falls on one tower: the New Church, where the princes of Orange are buried. Vermeer moved a few buildings to make the view more balanced. The writer Marcel Proust called it the most beautiful painting in the world.
